# Upstream / fast-fork inference source genealogy — round 395 v2

Date: 2026-10-13 Asia/Tokyo. This is a new supplemental audit. It corrects the scope of round395-v1 without changing that file or its evidence/status. Read-only Git and source review only; no build, tests, GPU, implementation, service, cleanup or Git changes. Current candidate reviewed: `6035c4f92bf87362d7e55051ae1375b9befba89e` in the yqYo1 canonical worktree. The user workspace `4fa478f50f8da396e651e3ae862f8b1849d49b54` is a separate `feature/sycl` checkout. Existing refs only; no fetch.

## Correction to v1

V1's conclusion “no matched faster-candidate evidence” was incomplete and its implication that the earlier faster rate was not substantiated was wrong. R394v2 pins a credible repeated same-binary, same-fixture, all-output-matching PR #6 32K layer-major A/B: three alternating pairs, 453.2935 tok/s baseline and 645.848 tok/s candidate medians. Its scope is precise: exact 32,768-token prompt; one greedy output token; fixed max context 65,538; all K/V resident; IQ3_S; 8,192 chunks; 128-slot per-layer cache; direct PLE; five CPU workers; same binary and fixture. It used `STRATA_PREFILL_COMPACT=2`, `STRATA_PREFILL_LAYER_MAJOR=1`, `STRATA_PREFILL_LAYER_MAJOR_R_GPU=32768`, no timers/markers and PLE preload off. All 248,320 logits and output token matched. The reported 29.814% wall-time reduction is established for that recipe. It is not a stock current-client comparison and the old one-token request does not give a decode result.

PR #8 is distinct 64K / 4,096-chunk evidence: instrumented single-run policy samples (largest retained cache+57,344 GPU residual tokens 519.73 tok/s; half release 532.53; full release/all 65,536 residual rows on GPU 539.76; full-release restore methods 542.30/542.13). Preserve these original values and status as diagnostic observations; they do not form a repeated median or controlled wall comparison. See pinned paths and detailed exact controls in `research-historical-performance-regression-round394-v2.txt`.

## Source genealogy: where the working route stops

The critical distinction is source identity and path, not a version string. The historical fast implementation is commit `f263d87d44aa671d056c33e6c6b6b0635fc25b8c` (“reuse expert layers and compact prefill scratch”) in the Niko1221/Strata tree under **`sycl/src/prefill/prefill.cpp`**. Current XeStrata HEAD builds from **top-level `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`**. The old topic commit is not an ancestor of current HEAD (`git merge-base f263d87d 6035c4f9` is `6f32ec070f23ced9f50e704d854d775da52591ab`; both diverge from that base). `f263d87d` is not a parent of the Xe update merge and cannot be assumed imported by a server/version update.

At old PR #6, the layer-major route exists at `sycl/src/prefill/prefill.cpp`: `Prefill::run()` selects `run_layer_major()` when `STRATA_PREFILL_LAYER_MAJOR` is set. The runner constrains the route to full single-GPU, compact FP16 fallback, a stable `ExpertSource`, all K/V resident (`kv_mode == 0`), and no PLE preload. It opens a one-layer device `ExpertCache`, stages/copies all 512 experts once, then applies `run_impl()` over all prompt chunks for that layer. It stores the intermediate FP32 residual between layers: a configurable complete prefix in device memory and remaining rows in host memory. This changes expert transfer scheduling from chunk-major (reloading the expert layers for each chunk) to layer-major (512 blobs once per layer, then all chunks), which is the measured source of the PR #6 win. The prompt GEMM/dequant/activation and combine work stays within the existing `run_impl` layer path; no change to decode is claimed.

The exact old optimization source is still present in Git history and pinned to the PR head, but not in the current active source tree. Current HEAD has no `STRATA_PREFILL_LAYER_MAJOR`, `run_layer_major`, `STRATA_PREFILL_LAYER_MAJOR_R_GPU`, or `STRATA_PREFILL_RELEASE_CACHE` route in active `src/` or `include/`. The old compact flag has different semantics today: current source has `STRATA_PREFILL_COMPACT_MOE_SCRATCH`, a per-chunk MoE scratch option requiring FP16 fallback/no MMQ. It is not the old compact whole-workspace + layer-major recipe.

The source selection boundary is the Strata→XeStrata engine-line switch, not the v0.1.43 server port. `c3aa33ae` (“upstream Strata 0.1.40.2 into Xe”, 2026-10-09) has parents `f8478f4e` and `e8ca9afd`; its tree is the first-parent root-level engine and has no top-level `sycl/` directory. The second-parent tree has a full `sycl/` subtree; comparing that parent to the result shows the subtree/source route is not carried forward and the active root `src/prefill/prefill.cpp` becomes the engine. The old `f263d87d` topic was not either parent (the second parent `e8ca9afd` is an earlier divergent tree and does not contain `STRATA_PREFILL_LAYER_MAJOR`). Thus the accurate statement is: the measured PR #6 implementation was developed on the parallel Niko fork topic under `sycl/`, while the XeStrata integration selected a different top-level engine source. The reviewed Git history does not show a later v0.1.43 merge deleting the layer-major implementation from current `src`; it was absent at the active source-line selection. `c3aa33ae` is the visible merge boundary at which the entire nested implementation tree is dropped in favor of root `src`, but because the PR #6 commit was outside its parents this is a branch/source-selection loss, not a commit-level deletion of `f263d87d` itself.

After `c3aa33ae`, Xe imports/ports upstream changes and eventually `0691bcdf` (v0.1.43 shared API/correctness/security functionality) and `c617512e` (server functionality). The latter server branch stays Python/setup/docs; it did not cause this prefill loss. Current `0f112782` and `6035c4f9` are later optional phase-cache/scratch changes and also do not restore layer-major. A direct source-only probe confirms the code absence, but does not establish which commit should be blamed for performance absent a matched current workload.

## Mechanism comparison at active source level

| Mechanism | Historical PR #6/#8 | Current 6035c4f9 | Audit conclusion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Prompt schedule | Layer-major across every chunk; 512 expert blobs loaded once/layer | Per-call `Prefill::run()` uses current chunk-major loop; no layer-major selector or runner | The measured expert-reuse schedule is missing. This is a concrete optimization capability loss and plausible cause of the recipe-specific prefill delta. |
| Compact storage | `STRATA_PREFILL_COMPACT=2`: compact scratch and layer-major diagnostic route | `STRATA_PREFILL_COMPACT_MOE_SCRATCH`: compact per-chunk FP16 MoE buffers; only if MMQ is absent | Similar name does not mean same algorithm or route. |
| K/V residency | Requires all allocated states `kv_mode==0`; PR #6 recipe pins K/V resident for context 65,538 | Current stock 32K control uses int8 K/V, physical context 262,144, resident 32,768; current phase path requires a different carefully bounded mode | Not comparable config; old engine cannot simply run its 64K recipe on the current 256K streaming policy. |
| Residual bridge | Intermediate `[n, D]` FP32 (`D=10,240`) held in host vector and optional device prefix; prefix rounded down to whole first/chunk blocks | No layer-major bridge. Current aliases concern per-chunk buffers, not the cross-layer `[n,D]` intermediate | For old 32K recipe, 32,768 device residual tokens require exactly 1,342,177,280 bytes (1.25 GiB) plus the temporary layer expert cache/workspace. The rest is host memory. |
| Decode-cache lending/release | PR #8 adds release/restore policy with cache-preserving virtual ownership and rebuild variants for capacity; measured only at 64K, 4K chunks, transfer instrumentation on, single runs | Current has phase-cache VMM experiment, but it is an optional phase decode expert cache with different owner/admission/serve-cycle implementation; no old `STRATA_PREFILL_RELEASE_CACHE` switch | Mechanism names/virtual memory do not imply behavioral equivalence. PR #8 needs separate port and exact 64K test. |
| Native MMQ | Old `compact_prefill()` can select compact mode only when `mmq_plan().fallback && !mmq_plan().any`; the reported compact/layer-major treatment is therefore the FP16 fallback path, not a native MMQ speed test | Current has `src/prefill/moe_mmq.cpp` plus `src/kernels/xe/iq_mmq.cpp`; default plan may use the native int8 MMQ route for supported layouts/types; `STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=0` forces fallback | Current has MMQ/native quant computation. It did not retain the historical layer-major orchestration; a fair schedule comparison must force MMQ off or port/adapt the old compact fallback before separately testing MMQ. |
| Native quant/decode CPU | PR #6 source change itself touches prefill/generation/header/profile only, not `src/kernels/cpu/*`; inherited native CPU/quant kernels are not the source of its measured win | Current retains AVX2 native IQ expert dispatch, with evolved/gather variants; current has IQ3_S decode and paired-GU opt-in from local `f2be61c0` | Native CPU paths were not wholesale removed. Exact kernels/pool source changed across upstream/backend evolution, so don't assert bit/source identity or unchanged performance. No paired CPU decode A/B here. |
| GPU format/compute path | Historical oneAPI/DPC++ SYCL port; MMQ disabled by compact route for the PR #6 measured treatment | Current Xe SYCL port has native IQ MMQ/other GEMM kernels and per-type selection; current stock benchmark is not a source-equivalent execution path | Native quant/MMQ exists, but it does not automatically compensate for additional expert uploads. |
| MTP/decode/speculation | PR #6 command carries `--spec 2` but metadata `mtp=null`, max-new is 1, so no meaningful speculative decode treatment is measured | `--mtp` requires explicit `--mtp`; 0f112 stock OFF control explicitly uses no MTP | PR #6 win is prefill only; no evidence the old decode path was faster within this measurement. |

## Native quant, MMQ, CPU SIMD and what is retained

PR #6's own source diff is four files (`sycl/src/prefill/prefill.cpp`, `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp`, its header, profiling helper); it does not alter CPU AVX2/native format decoding. Its `STRATA_PREFILL_COMPACT=2` experimental arm is gated to `!mmq_plan().any`, so its measured fast arm bypasses MMQ and uses the previous FP16-expert product path. The large prefill gain is therefore not evidence that IQ3_S native MMQ itself ran faster.

The current source has independently implemented/native quant MMQ in `src/kernels/xe/iq_mmq.cpp` (current cases include IQ2_XXS/XS/S, IQ3_XXS/S, IQ4_NL/XS, IQ1_M and Q2_0) and an MMQ adapter in `src/prefill/moe_mmq.cpp`. It is currently present, selected by `mmq_plan()` when built and shape/type eligible, unless `STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=0`. The current CPU AVX2 decoder still includes IQ3_S and dispatches native CPU expert jobs; current `expert_layout.cpp`, `pool.cpp`, `native_expert.cpp`, `iq_avx2.cpp`, and related tests differ materially from the common old root source (24 files changed in the old-commit-vs-current CPU path diff). This shows CPU SIMD/native path is present but evolved; the underlying rewrite cannot be dismissed as behaviorally identical. The local paired IQ3_S GU experiment is not required for current default and remains explicitly opt-in.

The historical upstream docs at `docs/SYCL_STATUS_2026-10-03.md` document a 17-format native MMQ/fused expert implementation in the prior Niko SYCL port. Current `src/kernels/xe/iq_mmq.cpp` has a narrower explicit type switch; don't use that old 17-format statement as evidence that every old route survived unchanged. For the IQ3_S benchmark model/layout, the current MMQ implementation has a direct IQ3_S case, but the historical compact winner bypassed it. So the candidate mechanism to restore is layer-major transfer reuse, not wholesale replacement of current quant kernels.

## Static port candidates and safety constraints

A useful source-only candidate is a new current `Prefill::run_layer_major` adapter behind a distinct opt-in, implemented against current SYCL `Runtime`/queue/Event abstractions and current `ExpertSource`/`ExpertCache` ownership. It should initially support only the historical narrowed contract: single-device full layer range, no helper/next/split/handoff, a stable source, no PLE preload, a fixed 8K chunk, all required K/V states resident and geometry checked, no simultaneous phase cache/cache lease, and a fixed same-source FP16 fallback (set MMQ off) while reproducing `compact=2`. Keep current native/MMQ/GEMM kernels untouched. Then test an equivalent layer-major MMQ-on variant as a separate hypothesis; don't conflate it with PR #6.

Porting the old routine verbatim is unsafe. It is DPCT/oneAPI-generated code using `dpct::queue_ptr`, `dpct::sync_barrier`, `sycl::free(ptr, queue)`, old callbacks (`on_chunk`, `on_stage_chunk`, `hand_in_`), old cache mapping (`ExpertCache::open_sized`), old `SessionState`/KV layouts, and pre-current `run_impl` assumptions. Current `Prefill` uses `core::Runtime`, explicit current workspaces/slot events, phase gates, scratch alias contracts, generation/source lifetimes and different ownership. The old RAII `Restore` drains queues/stager on destruction and restores callback/cache/residual pointers; a missing current equivalent can leave dangling stack `residency`, timer/callback pointers, incorrect `stage_lb_`/checkpoint state, or a UAF when cancellation/error returns. Old exception handling returns errors after queue waits; that lifetime rule and persistent session rollback must be preserved.

Potential arithmetic/placement hazards in the old code, to fix before any port:

- It multiplies `(size_t) gpu_tokens * D * sizeof(float)` and `(size_t)(n-gpu_tokens) * D` without explicit checked arithmetic. Current controlled model geometry bounds and `n <= 262144` make normal size known, but an exported API should validate `n`, `D`, multiplication and `vector::max_size()` before allocation.
- GPU residual rows are indexed by chunk-relative `row=position-pos0`; after the first layer, `hand_in_` changes to the complete bridge, and host-tail indexing subtracts `gpu_tokens`. Admission must prove `0 <= row`, `row+count <= n`, all positions belong to this prompt, and every token chunk is wholly on one side of the GPU/host boundary.
- Rounding deliberately keeps a complete prefix: after possible `STRATA_PREFILL_FIRST`, GPU token count is rounded down to whole `m.T` chunks. Do not round up. For `n=262144,D=10240`, an all-GPU bridge alone is 10 GiB (10,737,418,240 bytes); even the PR #6 32,768-row prefix is 1.25 GiB. On the measured 10-GiB B570, full 256K residual placement is impossible alongside model weights/cache/workspaces. With a 32K input/32K GPU prefix the measured recipe reserved 1.25 GiB before its layer expert-cache/workspace and full resident context K/V.
- The prefix request must be admitted against fresh free memory *after* model, current expert cache, K/V, workspace, graph and runtime allocations. A nominal VRAM fraction or total capacity is not enough. Preserve a fallback with zero/device-smaller whole-chunk prefix or reject cleanly before mutating session state.
- Layer-major resets/restores `ple_prev` each layer, serially advances `SessionState`, and emits checkpoint only after final layer; phase-cache/RESTORE/continuous-context/reused-prompt state needs explicit non-admission until full-state parity is established. Its all-KV-resident precondition excludes the current stock int8 resident32768/context262144 configuration; do not silently adapt by mutating only main-model KV while MTP/auxiliary states stream.
- It assumes layer expert bytes can be staged into one slot per all 512 experts and residency indexing `(layer * n_expert + expert)` is valid. Current variable blob sizes, selected expert-source mode, native/MMQ group buffers, selected MMQ/fallback allocation layout and source’s thread-safe/stable blob contract need validation. Only signal per-expert residency after copy completion; stop/cancel must drain copy and compute readers before the layer cache is retired.

## Evidence comparison and interpretation

The current quiet `bench.sh` run (0f112782 source) is 32,049 read tokens, 24 generated, int8 KV context 262,144/resident 32,768, 8K chunk, five workers/tasks18, no MTP/reuse. Its 3-run median is 384.8 prefill and 7.8 decode. The PR #6 old source is the closest historical 32K prefill case, but not directly comparable: 32,768 vs 32,049 tokens; one vs 24 output; direct custom GEN wall vs stock benchmark timing; context/KV and cache settings differ; MTP/spec flag differs syntactically (`--spec 2` but no draft and one output); source/compiler/binary/client differ; current default likely MMQ-on while old compact winner is MMQ-off. So retain both: PR #6 is strong evidence that a concrete old recipe was ~30% faster than its own baseline, and current stock is a different 384.8 row. The delta is a source-regression hypothesis, not a controlled 646→385 tok/s loss claim.

No single commit is proven as a runtime regression by existing A/B. The source capability loss is proven: the exact historical env-gated route and layer-major schedule are absent from active current source. The likely causal chain is selecting the XeStrata root-level engine source at c3aa33ae/its parent lineage without carrying the fast-fork `sycl/src` topic, then continuing only current chunk-major optimization work. The precise performance effect on current hardware must be established by matched campaign after a source review/port.

## Small safe validation path

First use the pinned PR #6 and #8 receipts already cited in the R394v2 report; do not rewrite their statuses. Build no claims from status-only receipts. A future reviewed source experiment should first reproduce PR #6 with its exact fixed context/chunk/cache/prompt and `max-new 1` under current engine; compare alternating baseline vs the opt-in layer-major fallback, same source/binary, same full-head/output checks, tracing and PLE preload off. Must set the current MMQ policy explicitly off on both arms to match old compact route; preserve a separate MMQ-on campaign afterward. Do PR #8 separately on exact 65,536/4K/context/cache policy with transfer tracing disabled for wall measurement, keeping old instrumented samples only as diagnostics. Only after successful numerical/state equivalence should the route admit larger 256K requests; determine GPU residual prefix from fresh headroom, retain a whole-chunk boundary and account for the host tail plus full resident K/V. These are future work, not changes performed in this source audit.
